cards.text: Last time, Samson went home burning with anger after his wedding feast, and his wife was given to one of the men who'd been with him. Now it's wheat harvest time. Samson heads off to visit his wife, and he brings a young goat along.

cards.question: Samson tells his wife's father he wants to go to his wife in her room. What does her father do?

answers.text: He will not let Samson enter
He calls his daughter to the door
He sends Samson out to the fields

cards.text: Her father says he was sure Samson thoroughly hated her, so he gave her to one of the men who'd been with him. Samson's standing there holding a goat, and friend, I've been in some awkward moments, but never one with a GOAT in it.

cards.question: Samson's wife is married to someone else now. What does her father offer Samson instead?
Samson speaks up about the Philistines. What does he say about doing them harm this time?

answers.text: He will be blameless in doing it
He will ask the LORD first
He will wait until the harvest ends

cards.text: Then Samson goes out and catches three hundred foxes. THREE HUNDRED, friend, and I can't even catch one chocolate chip rolling off my counter.

cards.question: Samson turns the foxes tail-to-tail in pairs. What does he fasten between each pair of tails?
Samson lights the torches tied to the foxes and lets them go. Where does he send them?

answers.text: Into the hill country of Judah

cards.question: True or false: The fire from Samson's foxes burns the Philistines' grain but stops before their vineyards and olive groves.

cards.text: The Philistines demand to know who did this. They're told it was Samson, the son-in-law of the Timnite, because his wife was given to his companion.

cards.question: Once they know it was Samson, the Philistines go up to Samson's wife and her father. What do they do?

answers.text: They drive them out of town

cards.question: True or false: After the Philistines burn his wife and her father, Samson tells them he will not rest until he has taken vengeance on them.

cards.text: And Samson strikes the Philistines ruthlessly, with a great slaughter.

cards.question: After striking down the Philistines, where does Samson go down to stay?

answers.text: A cave at the rock of Etam

cards.text: Now the Philistines come up and camp in Judah. They spread out near the town of Lehi. That's a whole army parked in your neighborhood, and I bet the men of Judah have some questions.

cards.question: The men of Judah ask the Philistines why they've attacked. What do the Philistines say they've come to do?

answers.text: Arrest Samson and pay him back

cards.text: So three thousand men of Judah go to the cave at the rock of Etam. When I got slid to the back of a junk drawer, nobody came looking at ALL, and these guys send THREE THOUSAND for one man.

cards.question: The men of Judah ask Samson, 'Do you not realize that the Philistines rule over us?' What does Samson tell them?

answers.text: He did to them what they did to him
The LORD told him to go after them
He is leaving Judah for good tomorrow

cards.text: Then the men of Judah tell Samson they've come down to arrest him and hand him over to the Philistines.

cards.question: Before he goes with the men of Judah, Samson asks them to swear something. What is it?

answers.text: They will not kill him themselves
They will tell his father and mother
They will let him keep his weapons

cards.question: The men of Judah agree not to kill Samson, but they tie him up securely. What do they bind him with?

cards.text: They lead Samson up from the rock to Lehi, and the Philistines come out shouting against him.

cards.question: True or false: When the Spirit of the LORD comes mightily upon Samson, the ropes on his arms hold tight and the Philistines take him away.

cards.text: The ropes on his arms become like burnt flax, and the bonds fall off his hands. Then Samson finds the fresh jawbone of a donkey, reaches out and grabs it.

cards.question: With that donkey's jawbone in his hand, how many men does Samson strike down?

cards.text: Then Samson says, "With the jawbone of a donkey I have piled them into heaps. With the jawbone of a donkey I have slain a thousand men." He says jawbone of a donkey in BOTH lines, friend, and when you've got a good batch, you bake it twice.

cards.question: When he finishes speaking, Samson throws the jawbone down. What does he do with that place?

cards.text: Then Samson gets very thirsty, so he cries out to the LORD. He says, 'You have accomplished this great deliverance through Your servant.'

cards.question: Samson has just told the LORD that He accomplished this great deliverance. What does a very thirsty Samson ask Him next?

answers.text: Whether he must now die of thirst
Whether he can go back home now

cards.question: Samson cries out to the LORD in his thirst. How does God answer him?

answers.text: He opens a hollow place and water comes out
He sends rain down on the town of Lehi
He leads Samson to the Jordan River

cards.question: True or false: When Samson drinks the water God gives, his strength returns and he is revived.

cards.text: Samson names that spot En-hakkore, and it's still there in Lehi to this day.

cards.question: After all this, how long does Samson judge Israel in the days of the Philistines?

cards.text: Set that timer, friend, because Samson's story is NOT done yet.
